Comments (English): [ Improve your quality of life, save time, and enjoy a dishwasher with great cleaning power. ] || ---------------- || I love doing dishes, but I never really felt the need for a dishwasher. My husband hates it, so I ended up doing it all myself, and even though we both work, I was getting tired of housework. I'd heard so many people talking about how great dishwashers were, so I decided to give it a try and ended up choosing the Media 2-3-person dishwasher. To cut to the chase, even I, who never particularly disliked washing dishes, was immediately captivated by how thoroughly it cleaned them. It usually takes about 20-30 minutes to do a single dish, but since I do it twice a day, I save several hours a week. It's incredibly rewarding to have more time for myself! Dishwasher detergent is sold separately, but the recommended dosage is 6g, so buy the appropriate product! It's perfect for a 2-3 person household and comes with a generous portion. It was nice to be able to add a stand for milk bottles and small dishes. <Installation Instructions>. It was easy for a woman to install on her own, but it was heavier than I expected, so the only challenge was getting it on the sink. After that, the rest of the installation was easy. First, after emptying all the contents, attach the drain hose to the drain at the back. It comes with a clipper to secure the hose in place, so make sure to tighten it as tightly as possible! You can also choose between manual or automatic water supply, but I didn't see that in the manual, so I did a lot of searching. Manual water supply is done by inserting the included drip tray and water container into the water inlet hole at the top. <Automatic water supply installation instructions>. The automatic water supply hose is also included, so you can connect it to the sink faucet for automatic water supply, just like a washing machine. We had a water purifier that we had previously discontinued, so the leftover hose was connected to the sink faucet. By attaching the water purifier connection part (typically a 15A male thread, 6mm - 21mm), you can install the automatic water supply yourself. The part hasn't arrived yet, but if you search online, you'll find many automatic water supply installation methods for many people who use Media dishwashers. Find the right one for you. ***Update***. The automatic water supply installation was successful! It works perfectly, and compared to manually filling the water tank, it saves a lot of time, and the faster water supply has greatly improved my quality of life! I highly recommend trying the automatic water supply! <Instructions>. It's said that placing dishes so they don't touch each other helps prevent breakage. Also, placing dishes at an angle ensures that water flows out from the top and bottom, which helps clean them well. Cups, spoons, and chopsticks are also washed well. Be careful not to insert sharp objects into the dishwasher, as this can cause damage! 1. Reason for purchase: - To improve my quality of life. - Because dishwashing chores were becoming more and more burdensome. - Because I wanted to save even a little time. - Because I wanted to get rid of housewife's eczema. 2. Pros and Features: - Excellent cleaning power. - Holds more than you'd think. - It's not incredibly noisy, as it's less noisy than a washing machine. - It saves water. People usually use a lot more water when washing dishes. Since it washes everything with just 5-6L, I can save water and reduce environmental pollution! - It washes much more thoroughly than when I wash it myself. - Easy for even a woman to install. - It can be installed with automatic water supply as well as manual water supply. 3. Comments (Original): [ 삶의 질 향상 내 시간 확보 세척력 좋은 식기세척기 ] || ---------------- || 설거지하는 것을 좋아해서 딱히 식기세척기에 대한 필요성을 느끼지 못했었던 1인입니다.신랑이 설거지를 싫어해서, 제가 다 도맡아서 하다보니 맞벌이인데 점차 집안일에 지쳐가고 있었습니다.주변에서 식기세척기가 정말 좋다는 이야기들을 많이 들어서, 식기세척기를 한 번 써볼까 생각하고 미디어 2~3인용 식기세척기를 선택하게 되었는데요.결론부터 말씀드리면, 처음 쓰자마자 설거지를 딱히 싫어하지 않았던 저조차도 더 깨끗하게 설거지를 해주는 식세기에 반해버렸습니다.보통 설거지 한 번 하면 20~30분 정도 소요되는데, 많으면 하루에 2번 정도 설거지를 하기 때문에, 1주일로 했을때 몇시간의 시간을 줄일 수 있게 됩니다.내 시간을 더 가질 수 있으니 이보다 더 좋을 수 없어요!식기세척기용 세제는 따로 구매해야하는데, 적정용량이 6g 이므로, 이에 맞춰서 나온 제품으로 구매하시면 되요!2~3인 가구가 쓰기 매우 적합하고, 구성도 알차게 되어있습니다.우유병을 넣을 수 있는 거치대, 작은 그릇들을 올릴 수 있게 추가로 설치해서 사용하도록 되어 있어서 좋았습니다.<설치방법>여자 혼자 설치하기도 쉬웠는데, 생각보다 무거워서 싱크대 위에 올려놓는 것만 힘들었지, 그 후에 설치하는 것은 쉬웠습니다.제일 먼저, 안에 있는 내용물을 다 꺼낸 뒤에, 배수호스를 뒤에 배수부분에 연결합니다.혹시나 배수호스가 빠지지 않도록 고정할 수 있는 클리퍼가 같이 오기 때문에, 최대한 꽉 조여서 고정시켜주세요!그리고 수동급수, 자동급수를 선택하여 설치할 수 있는데, 설명서에 나와있지 않아서 폭풍검색을 했어요.수동급수는 같이 동봉된 물받이와 물통으로 상단에 위치한 물 급수 구멍에 넣어주면 되는데요.<자동급수 설치 방법>자동급수 호스도 같이 오기 때문에, 세탁기처럼 연결해서 자동급수를 사용할 수 있어요.저희 집에는 예전에 정수기 사용하다가 안 쓰게 되서 남은 정수기 호스가 싱크대 수전에 연결이 되어 있었는데요.그 부분에 정수기 연결 부속(수나사 보통 15A, 6mm - 21mm)를 연결하면 자동급수 설치도 혼자 설치할 수 있습니다.아직 부품이 오지 않았는데, 인터넷에 검색해보면 미디어 식기세척기를 사용하는 사람들이 많아 자동급수 설치하는 방법들이 다양하게 나와있으니 딱맞는 방법으로 설치하시면 될 것 같아요.***업데이트***자동급수 설치 성공했습니다!! 작동이 아주 잘 되고, 직접 물통으로 수동급수하는 것보다 시간도 엄청 단축되고 빨리 급수되니 삶의 질이 더욱 향상되었어요!! 자동급수 설치 꼭 도전해보시길 강추합니다!<사용방법>그릇은 서로 닿지 않도록 넣어주는 것이 깨지지 않는데 도움이 된다고 해요.또 그릇 방향을 비스듬하게 넣어야, 위아래로 물이 나오기 때문에 세척이 잘 됩니다.컵도 잘 씻겨지고, 숟가락 젓가락도 아주 잘 세척됩니다.조심해야하는 점은, 날카로운 물체는 넣지 말아야 해요. 고장날 수도 있어요!1. 구매이유 - 삶의 질 향상을 위해서- 설거지 집안일이 점차 버겁게 느껴져서- 내 시간을 조금이라도 아끼고 싶어서- 주부습진에서 벗어나고 싶어서2. 장점 및 특징- 세척력이 좋음- 생각보다 많이 들어감- 소음이 세탁기보다 적은 정도라 엄청 크진 않음- 물을 아낄 수 있음. 보통 설거지하면 물을 훨씬 더 많이 쓴다고 해요. 5~6L로 다 세척해주니까 물도 아낄 수 있어 환경오염이 적습니다!- 내가 세척하는 것보다 훨씬 깨끗하게 세척됨- 여자 혼자서도 설치하기 쉬움- 수동급수 뿐만 아니라 자동급수로 설치하는 것이 가능함3. 단점딱히 없습니다.저의 리뷰가 도움이 되셨다면, 정말 좋겠습니다:)도움이 되셨다면 ♥도움이돼요♥ 버튼 꾹 눌러주세요! 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Comments (Original): [ 삶의 질 향상 내 시간 확보 세척력 좋은 식기세척기 ] || ---------------- || 설거지하는 것을 좋아해서 딱히 식기세척기에 대한 필요성을 느끼지 못했었던 1인입니다.신랑이 설거지를 싫어해서, 제가 다 도맡아서 하다보니 맞벌이인데 점차 집안일에 지쳐가고 있었습니다.주변에서 식기세척기가 정말 좋다는 이야기들을 많이 들어서, 식기세척기를 한 번 써볼까 생각하고 미디어 2~3인용 식기세척기를 선택하게 되었는데요.결론부터 말씀드리면, 처음 쓰자마자 설거지를 딱히 싫어하지 않았던 저조차도 더 깨끗하게 설거지를 해주는 식세기에 반해버렸습니다.보통 설거지 한 번 하면 20~30분 정도 소요되는데, 많으면 하루에 2번 정도 설거지를 하기 때문에, 1주일로 했을때 몇시간의 시간을 줄일 수 있게 됩니다.내 시간을 더 가질 수 있으니 이보다 더 좋을 수 없어요!식기세척기용 세제는 따로 구매해야하는데, 적정용량이 6g 이므로, 이에 맞춰서 나온 제품으로 구매하시면 되요!2~3인 가구가 쓰기 매우 적합하고, 구성도 알차게 되어있습니다.우유병을 넣을 수 있는 거치대, 작은 그릇들을 올릴 수 있게 추가로 설치해서 사용하도록 되어 있어서 좋았습니다.<설치방법>여자 혼자 설치하기도 쉬웠는데, 생각보다 무거워서 싱크대 위에 올려놓는 것만 힘들었지, 그 후에 설치하는 것은 쉬웠습니다.제일 먼저, 안에 있는 내용물을 다 꺼낸 뒤에, 배수호스를 뒤에 배수부분에 연결합니다.혹시나 배수호스가 빠지지 않도록 고정할 수 있는 클리퍼가 같이 오기 때문에, 최대한 꽉 조여서 고정시켜주세요!그리고 수동급수, 자동급수를 선택하여 설치할 수 있는데, 설명서에 나와있지 않아서 폭풍검색을 했어요.수동급수는 같이 동봉된 물받이와 물통으로 상단에 위치한 물 급수 구멍에 넣어주면 되는데요.<자동급수 설치 방법>자동급수 호스도 같이 오기 때문에, 세탁기처럼 연결해서 자동급수를 사용할 수 있어요.저희 집에는 예전에 정수기 사용하다가 안 쓰게 되서 남은 정수기 호스가 싱크대 수전에 연결이 되어 있었는데요.그 부분에 정수기 연결 부속(수나사 보통 15A, 6mm - 21mm)를 연결하면 자동급수 설치도 혼자 설치할 수 있습니다.아직 부품이 오지 않았는데, 인터넷에 검색해보면 미디어 식기세척기를 사용하는 사람들이 많아 자동급수 설치하는 방법들이 다양하게 나와있으니 딱맞는 방법으로 설치하시면 될 것 같아요.***업데이트***자동급수 설치 성공했습니다!! 작동이 아주 잘 되고, 직접 물통으로 수동급수하는 것보다 시간도 엄청 단축되고 빨리 급수되니 삶의 질이 더욱 향상되었어요!! 자동급수 설치 꼭 도전해보시길 강추합니다!<사용방법>그릇은 서로 닿지 않도록 넣어주는 것이 깨지지 않는데 도움이 된다고 해요.또 그릇 방향을 비스듬하게 넣어야, 위아래로 물이 나오기 때문에 세척이 잘 됩니다.컵도 잘 씻겨지고, 숟가락 젓가락도 아주 잘 세척됩니다.조심해야하는 점은, 날카로운 물체는 넣지 말아야 해요. 고장날 수도 있어요!1. 구매이유 - 삶의 질 향상을 위해서- 설거지 집안일이 점차 버겁게 느껴져서- 내 시간을 조금이라도 아끼고 싶어서- 주부습진에서 벗어나고 싶어서2. 장점 및 특징- 세척력이 좋음- 생각보다 많이 들어감- 소음이 세탁기보다 적은 정도라 엄청 크진 않음- 물을 아낄 수 있음. 보통 설거지하면 물을 훨씬 더 많이 쓴다고 해요. 5~6L로 다 세척해주니까 물도 아낄 수 있어 환경오염이 적습니다!- 내가 세척하는 것보다 훨씬 깨끗하게 세척됨- 여자 혼자서도 설치하기 쉬움- 수동급수 뿐만 아니라 자동급수로 설치하는 것이 가능함3. 단점딱히 없습니다.저의 리뷰가 도움이 되셨다면, 정말 좋겠습니다:)도움이 되셨다면 ♥도움이돼요♥ 버튼 꾹 눌러주세요! 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): This is my first time using a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Honest Pros and Cons of a 3-Person House for Couples (Additional Photos) ] || ---------------- || This is my first time using a dishwasher. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. Comments (English): [ Honest Pros and Cons of a 3-Person House for Couples (Additional Photos) ] || ---------------- || This is my first time using a dishwasher. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable.
