I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. Comments (English): [ Honest Pros and Cons of a 3-Person House for Couples (Additional Photos) ] || ---------------- || This is my first time using a dishwasher. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. Comments (English): [ Honest Pros and Cons of a 3-Person House for Couples (Additional Photos) ] || ---------------- || This is my first time using a dishwasher. I've heard dishwashers are good, but since it's a rented, old apartment, there's no built-in dishwasher, and the kitchen is only about 21 pyeong (approximately 70 square meters). I hadn't even considered a dishwasher, but since it's a three-person, non-punched dishwasher, I figured it would work, so I gave it a try. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. The detergent in the general necessities section was around 3,000 won for 600g. While looking for something cheaper, I found a no-brand detergent for the same amount for 3,000 won! It's a bit pricey, but 3,000 won for 60 washes is a no-brainer. I think it'll handle the dishwasher well. My baby seems to be good at washing bottles, so I've just stopped using them. It's a shame. We used to wash over 10 bottles a day. It would be a great gift or purchase for a baby bottle washer. I think this product would become a must-have for new mothers, more so than a formula pot. After using it, I'm very satisfied with the performance, design, and finish at this price point. I highly recommend it. If you found my honest review helpful, please let me know! Please. Additional review. I purchased a traditional Korean-style dishwasher-safe bowl instead of a dishwasher-safe one. Stacking them without overlapping is incredibly difficult. Flat bowls, chopsticks, and simple cups are fine, but if you add dishes with grooves or soup bowls, the space isn't great. It's fine for two people who run the dishwasher for every meal. For those who run it once a day, I recommend it for a single person who eats at home. For single- or two-person households who immediately wash dishes, the convenience won't be as noticeable. Another drawback I noticed is that, perhaps because it's a powdered detergent, a lot of powder remains at the bottom of the dishwasher, just like powdered detergent in a washing machine. The non-punched design makes it easy to install, which is nice. It's easy to move with, and my husband and I are both clumsy. Just read the instructions once and follow them. It installed flawlessly and we've already used it a few times. Since we use a lot of spoons and plates, we keep a large frying pan, pot, and side dish container separate, and just a simple set of cups, plates, and spoons. I thought a three-person dishwasher would only need to be used once a day, but I find myself having to use it after every meal. I think the three-person standard is more geared toward international use than domestic use. It's a bit difficult to stack Korean soup bowls without them closing. With just a flat plate and chopsticks, it could probably feed three or more people. On weekdays, I mostly just use plates and spoons, and my husband only cooks rice once at night. Since I keep the dishwasher-safe portions separate, I think I could probably do it once a day. I wash dishes a lot, so I use a lot of water and tend to spend a lot of time washing them, but now I can just do a large batch at once, which definitely saves time. Here are some pros and cons I've noticed: 1. You have to fill the water every time you turn it on. We don't have a faucet, so we end up pouring water into the large cup that comes with it about three times. 2. You can't adjust the placement or pillars of the dishes, so you have to be careful not to overlap them. If you don't, you won't be able to fit as many dishes as you think. 3. One hour on standard mode might seem excessive considering the amount of dishes you wash, but if it's worth the extra time and the lower electricity bill, it's worth considering. But it definitely uses less water than I do. I also use the exact amount of detergent, so I don't overuse it, which I think is good for the environment. At my house, the dishwasher needs a lot of foam to feel like it's cleaning properly, so using just a little detergent was difficult. Also, it would have been nice if there was a mechanism to open the lid only halfway after washing the dishes, but it only opens wide. In my small kitchen, it's quite inconvenient to leave it open. It's also quite noisy, like having a washing machine right next to you, so I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who's sensitive to noise. I recommend running it before you go out. In my house, we often have the TV on, music on, and the sound of rain falling, so the sound of the dishwasher spinning isn't too loud. In fact, the sound of the water running at even intervals is pleasant to hear. Other than that, the design is better than I expected. The power cord and drain hose are long, so as long as it doesn't break, I think it'll last a while. And since it was my first dishwasher, I didn't know whether to use powder, liquid, or tablet detergent, but... Since the detergent just drips inside once you add it and close the door, it doesn't matter what you use as long as you get the right amount. I thought the detergent was included as a sample, but when I tried to use it, all I had was the included dehumidifier, so I quickly went to E-Mart and bought some. Sentence (English): Overall I guess we're more happy than unhappy with our new Bosch dishwasher, although if we had it to do over again we'd probably buy another brand.
Comments (English): [ Some good, some bad ] || ---------------- || Overall I guess we're more happy than unhappy with our new Bosch dishwasher, although if we had it to do over again we'd probably buy another brand. First, the good. It does a good job cleaning the dishes, silverware, and pots and pans. That's what it's all about, right? So I have no complaint. It has failed to clean the bottom of 5-8 quart large stainless steel soup pots. I'm surmising that its jets just aren't strong enough to reach the bottom of the upside down pots with a strong enough jet to dislodge the cooked on food. Oh well. That doesn't happen often. Everything else it cleans well. It's quiet, although so are its competitors. A decibel or two won't matter to most of us, especially if it's set to run while we're sleeping. We really, really like the top silverware rack. It's fun to load, and unloading is almost a pleasure since it's at roughly the same height as our silverware cabinet drawer. This was a surprise. I knew it was a feature; I just didn't expect to like it as much as we do. I like the sanitize cycle. It's hardly unique to Bosch; nearly everybody has that. The 20-year-old Kenmore this replaced had it. But still, it's a good feature. OK, I guess that's about it with the positives. The negatives: 1. We spent $100 ($150? ) more for this model than the one below it, primarily for the feature where it opens the door at the end of the cycle to facilitate better drying. Well, it doesn't work. First of all, Bosch illogically ships the unit with that feature turned off! The one model in their line-up with the feature, and somebody makes the brilliant decision to disable it so you think the product is defective. It has an option button to push to select the feature, but that has no effect. So I poured through the manual and found the arcane 1970s-era menu that lets you press odd sequences of buttons in particular orders to access and change features. So I finally figured out how to turn the door opening feature on. And I double-checked to ensure I really set the feature back on. Then when I ran the next cycle, it still didn't work. No matter what we do, the door doesn't open at the end of a cycle. So I tried contacting Bosch, expecting for a person to be available to talk to, or some questions if I'd done it right, etc. Nope. 24 hours later I get a form "letter" email that tells me who to contact for service. That company's web site makes you commit to paying them at least $165 for the service call UNLESS it's covered under warranty and not due to something I did. Well, I guess I'll call anyway, but no way would I pay them for the call, no matter what the repair person said. Not happy about the door opener not working in a brand new unit, nor about Bosch's lack of effort to reach out to me about the problem. The other major beef is the horrendous stainless steel front on the dishwasher. It is as bad an implementation of stainless steel as I've seen. In contrast, we bought a new LG refrigerator at the same time we bought the Bosch dishwasher. It is nearly impossible to leave a fingerprint on the LG. It is nearly impossible NOT to leave TONS of fingerprints on the Bosch. For this reason, we regret buying a Bosch dishwasher. If we had it to do over again, we'd have bought an LG. Oh well, we're stuck with this fingerprint magnet. Hard to believe Bosch has no clue how to buy fingerprint-resistant stainless steel. Lastly, a minor complaint. Our previous dishwasher (and most others I've owned over the past 50 years, had more efficient racks, primarily the middle one used for glasses, cups, mugs, and bowls. It is hard to get even 2/3 as much in it as it was in my Kenmore. It's just not designed all that well. We're still figuring out the ideal way to load, so we might get more efficient with time. We just run the Bosch a little more often than we ran its predecessor since it doesn't hold as much. At least it's quiet. If only the door opened automatically like it's supposed to. At least the dishes dry reasonably well even without opening the door. I'd be OK without the door-opening feature if we hadn't paid $100 (or $150, I forget) for it. So, I guess that's it. If you wear white cloth gloves whenever you touch the door, you'll probably be happy. Otherwise, I strongly suggest another brand, or some other Bosch finish besides stainless steel, because the SS looks horrible. It's even hard to clean off the fingerprints, let alone avoid them in the first place.

We spent $100 ($150? ) more for this model than the one below it, primarily for the feature where it opens the door at the end of the cycle to facilitate better drying. Well, it doesn't work. First of all, Bosch illogically ships the unit with that feature turned off! The one model in their line-up with the feature, and somebody makes the brilliant decision to disable it so you think the product is defective. It has an option button to push to select the feature, but that has no effect. So I poured through the manual and found the arcane 1970s-era menu that lets you press odd sequences of buttons in particular orders to access and change features. So I finally figured out how to turn the door opening feature on. And I double-checked to ensure I really set the feature back on. Then when I ran the next cycle, it still didn't work. No matter what we do, the door doesn't open at the end of a cycle. So I tried contacting Bosch, expecting for a person to be available to talk to, or some questions if I'd done it right, etc. Nope. 24 hours later I get a form "letter" email that tells me who to contact for service. That company's web site makes you commit to paying them at least $165 for the service call UNLESS it's covered under warranty and not due to something I did. Well, I guess I'll call anyway, but no way would I pay them for the call, no matter what the repair person said. Not happy about the door opener not working in a brand new unit, nor about Bosch's lack of effort to reach out to me about the problem. The other major beef is the horrendous stainless steel front on the dishwasher. It is as bad an implementation of stainless steel as I've seen. In contrast, we bought a new LG refrigerator at the same time we bought the Bosch dishwasher. It is nearly impossible to leave a fingerprint on the LG. It is nearly impossible NOT to leave TONS of fingerprints on the Bosch. For this reason, we regret buying a Bosch dishwasher. If we had it to do over again, we'd have bought an LG. Oh well, we're stuck with this fingerprint magnet. Hard to believe Bosch has no clue how to buy fingerprint-resistant stainless steel. Lastly, a minor complaint. Our previous dishwasher (and most others I've owned over the past 50 years, had more efficient racks, primarily the middle one used for glasses, cups, mugs, and bowls. It is hard to get even 2/3 as much in it as it was in my Kenmore. It's just not designed all that well. We're still figuring out the ideal way to load, so we might get more efficient with time. At least the dishes dry reasonably well even without opening the door. I'd be OK without the door-opening feature if we hadn't paid $100 (or $150, I forget) for it. So, I guess that's it. If you wear white cloth gloves whenever you touch the door, you'll probably be happy. Otherwise, I strongly suggest another brand, or some other Bosch finish besides stainless steel, because the SS looks horrible. It's even hard to clean off the fingerprints, let alone avoid them in the first place.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Simple, powerful, silent, and elegant. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher a month ago. I did a lot of research and looked at a lot of reviews. I was deciding between the Bosche 300 series or this. At first I wasn't concerned about the sound factor of a new dishwasher but I decided that it was more important then I initially thought due to my close television area. It was the right move. This washer is so quiet… it's 39 dB was a huge difference from our original 10 year old GE with 50+ dB of sound. My wife and I are blown away by how much cleaner the dishes have been (even when I used to clean and maintain our old dishwasher). The only factors I think could make this even better are found in more premium models or brands. For one… the racks inside can be more adjustable (found in higher kitchen aid models). This is a minor issue for my family and not enough to stop me from being happy of our purchase. The other factor is the automatic open feature of some premium brands really aids in drying the dishes further. This can simply be solved by manually opening the washer after use. All in all… I have purchased a refrigerator and dishwasher from Kitchen Aid and I couldn't be more happy with the quality and appearance of the product. I really think they have stepped up their game over the past few years. Well done! I would recommend this product to all of my friends and family (one family member actually purchased the same one).

Sentence (English): When our older portable died we purchased this item locally so we could replace it same day.
Comments (English): [ Cleans Well. Very Quiet. Extremely Poor Design. ] || ---------------- || When our older portable died we purchased this item locally so we could replace it same day. Although portable choices are limited, this purchase was, in many ways, a mistake. Our older GE unit was, in many ways, more versatile and user-friendly. First, this unit has no heated dry cycle. You have to crack the door open IMMEDIATELY at the end of the wash cycle to use the condensate dry system. This kind of works, but who wants to hang around until the non-adjustable wash cycle is over and the door doesn't like to stay open. Speaking of wash cycles, you get a choice of three and cannot adjust time after selecting one. Speaking of time, the control panel is buried under the door top and you can't see anything after you start it. The instructions say that the wash cycle is over when the finished light comes on BUT YOU CANT SEE THE THING WITH THE DOOR CLOSED and the light goes out when the door is opened. Great job GE! Now for the racks. More poor design. If you're washing plates and silverware you're fine. Bowls? Nope. Can't place them sideways. Pots? Pans? Forget it. No movable tines to create a large enough space. GE needs to offer an optional bottom rack with better spacing. All in all, even though the thing gets stuff clean and is super quiet, I strongly recommend that you find another alternative.

We literally had to prewash everything before running through a wash cycle. But we decided not to replace it until absolutely necessary, and that happened a couple of months ago. Looked at a bunch of different brands and models before deciding on this one.And what a difference this one made. First off, it's super quiet compared to our old dishwasher. And second, unlike our previous model, this one actually has the capability of cleaning dirty dishes. Bonus points for its automatic mode and the delay function. While it's possible to watch TV while this one is running (the old one, you wouldn't be able to hear anything), it is nice to set it to run later in the evening when everyone is in bed.All in all, we're extremely happy with our purchase and believe, after a couple of months of use, that we made the right choice. We'll definitely be looking to Bosch for other appliances as those needs arise.

Sentence (English): Overall, happy with DW.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well ] || ---------------- || Overall, happy with DW.PROS: It cleans well, not super loud, easy to move, decent cleaning options. Comparing it to my previous built-in, the functionality is pretty similar. Hose & power cord lengths are good. I haven't had any issues getting them out of or back into the DW.CONS: HUGE design flaw with the hidden control panel. GE really needs to redo. Once door is closed, you are not able to see the time left without opening the door or to cancel cycle you must open the door (opening the door is required for everything). Wow…someone missed the mark there. The sanitize option is looong compared to my previous built-in. I no longer use because the DW cleans just fine on regular autosense setting. Tub is a bit small & the racks are configured a little weird so putting dishes in takes some creativity. The silverware basket is HORRIBLE. The individual slots are very tiny so some things won't fit through the basket topper. The toppers are removable & the basket is decent sized. However, another design flaw is basket placement. It will only sit in one corner & there is nothing to hold it in place so it does shift. Very odd.I have no complaints about the condensation dry. It works as GE says if you give it some time. I use rinse aid & let the DW sit for a few minutes once it's done. I open the door just a crack to let some moisture escape & leave it that way for at least 15 minutes. I then partially open the door to let the rest of the moisture & heat out & after another 15-20 minutes, the dishes are 95-99% dry…even plastics. My previous built-in couldn't do any better.The price is a bit steep IMO, but as long as it continues to work well it's money well spent.

It took less than a week from order to installation! I have a child in the middle of the day, so I'm going to go to work, and I'm going to have a hard day repeating . Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

It took less than a week from order to installation! I have a child in the middle of the day, so I'm going to go to work, and I'm going to have a hard day repeating . Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

Comments (English): [ I got a dishwasher at a good price :) 1 week from order to installation. ] || ---------------- || I got a dishwasher at a good price :) . It took less than a week from order to installation! I have a child in the middle of the day, so I'm going to go to work, and I'm going to have a hard day repeating . Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

Comments (English): [ I got a dishwasher at a good price :) 1 week from order to installation. ] || ---------------- || I got a dishwasher at a good price :) . It took less than a week from order to installation! I have a child in the middle of the day, so I'm going to go to work, and I'm going to have a hard day repeating . Especially on the kid's tumbler, my tumbler, my husband's tumbler, and the kids tableware that I use every day. There is no end in sight of the cups and dishes being washed. I decided to buy a dishwasher because I couldn't play enough with the child I wanted to see throughout the day because I was washing the dishes after eating! I bought it after visiting Samsung Digital Plaza and listening to the meticulous explanation. After canceling the order due to an order error, I went to the Samsung Mall and even used a coupon to get it at a better price! This time, it comes in a large capacity, and the water filter is also built-in, so I bought it without hesitation because I thought it would be easy to manage :) . I listened to the reviews of my baby mother friends who said the performance was better than before and used it. It washed the dishes really clean! Does it take too long at first? I wanted to, but anyway, if you put the dishwasher back and take care of your child . That time passed quickly! What I liked the first time I used it was that it was convenient and clean, but isn't it a bit uncomfortable for me, who prefers transparent bowls and cups with water marks? I actually thought about it a lot. So I used the dishwasher rinse and that part was solved right away! Since there is a drying function, you can use it right away without having to take the dishes out of the washing machine and wipe them again, which was nice too! It is said that drying dishes is important for hygiene, so I make sure to add this part and use it! And most of all, aesthetics are very important, and it was nice not to mess with the kitchen interior! I ordered it in the 'beige' color among the satin beige/white that came out this time, and my kitchen is white, but it suits me well! I think I might be able to move in a year or two, so I chose beige to pick a color that would look good wherever I go :) . The person who installs the dishwasher cabinet said that since it was to be used with an induction stove, it was necessary to raise the induction stove a little, so we paid extra for that part and built it. It was a simpler construction than I thought, and it took about an hour, so it was completed quickly! Delivery also arrived exactly on the date I set, so I was able to use it without any inconvenience :) . The technician who installs the kitchen cabinet and the electric appliance technician install it while trying to balance it here and there to see if the sum fits well, so the name is perfect for the kitchen! This is done! Actually, I liked that part the most! :) . I didn't want to give up a tidy kitchen for a dishwasher. I'm so satisfied with installing and using it, so I like that my husband can wash the dishes more comfortably after work in the future ^^ . My couple is so satisfied and experiencing a new world ^^ . #Samsung event #bespoke dishwasher

After years of juggling various household chores, especially dishes, I've always dreamed of a dishwasher. Luckily, I had the chance to try it out, so I chose it. The Media Mini dishwasher is rated for 3 people, so I was worried it might be too small. It's bigger than I thought, but it's not as small as other dishwashers. Larger dishwashers can be space-constrained, and if they're too big, you'll have to run the dishwasher when you have a smaller load. I wanted to experience the new world of dishwashers before buying a large one, as I was a little hesitant about the hassle of having to wash dishes by hand. And now I have a mini-sized dishwasher that's just the perfect size. * The Media Mini dishwasher requires you to plug it in before adding water. When I put dishes in, I noticed that concave dishes like rice and soup bowls take up a lot of space. After years of juggling various household chores, especially dishes, I've always dreamed of a dishwasher. Luckily, I had the chance to try it out, so I chose it. Larger dishwashers can be space-constrained, and if they're too big, you'll have to run the dishwasher when you have a smaller load. I wanted to experience the new world of dishwashers before buying a large one, as I was a little hesitant about the hassle of having to wash dishes by hand. And now I have a mini-sized dishwasher that's just the perfect size. * The Media Mini dishwasher requires you to plug it in before adding water.
